findings.body: The original `use openhuman_core::openhuman as oh;` imports the *module* `openhuman` from the crate `openhuman_core` and aliases it as `oh`. The change to `use openhuman_core as oh;` aliases the crate itself as `oh`, which means `oh::agent::dispatcher` now resolves to `openhuman_core::agent::dispatcher` — a path that does not exist (the submodules live under `openhuman_core::openhuman::agent::dispatcher`). This will cause a compilation error on every use of `oh::` items in this file. The fix is to revert to the original import or to change the alias to something that preserves the original path.
findings.existing_code:
-use openhuman_core::openhuman as oh;
+use openhuman_core as oh;
findings.title: Replace the import alias so the crate path resolves

value.summary: The change renames the `use openhuman_core::openhuman as oh;` import to `use openhuman_core as oh;`, which will fail to compile because `openhuman_core` is a crate, not a module providing the `oh::agent::dispatcher` path. This breaks every subsequent reference to `oh::` items.
